cities.base: Water villa or beach villa resort, the only base for this trip, everything is a boat ride from here.
cities.name: South Male Atoll Resort

cities.base: Uninhabited sandbar, day trip only, no beds, bring your own shade.
cities.name: Sandbank / picnic island

cities.base: Manta/turtle snorkel or two-tank dive site, day trip only from the resort.
cities.name: Outer reef site

places.name: House reef entry point
places.note: Free and unlimited, but reef health varies wildly by resort, ask before you book which rating they actually have; some house reefs here are dead coral rubble.

places.name: Resort spa
places.note: Genuinely good treatments, priced like Manhattan rather than a beach town.

places.name: Overwater or sandbank private dinner
places.note: Worth doing once as a set piece, not a restaurant to repeat every night.

places.name: Sandbank picnic island
places.note: Just sand and water, no shade provided, bring your own.

places.name: Outer reef excursion site
places.note: Manta and turtle sightings are seasonal and never guaranteed, check the season for this atoll first.

places.name: Dolphin sunset cruise route
places.note: Wild dolphins, no guarantee they show, no refunds when they don't.

places.name: Sunset fishing dhoni
places.note: Traditional boat, evening light, catch is usually not yours to keep.

places.name: Resort House Reef
places.note: Free and unlimited, but quality varies wildly resort to resort, some house reefs are now dead coral rubble. Ask the dive desk for the current reef health rating before you count on it, and go at slack tide when current is weakest and fish activity is still high.

places.name: Outer Reef Snorkel/Dive Site, South Male Atoll
places.note: 30-60 min boat ride out. $80-120pp snorkel only, $150-220pp two-tank dive with gear. Manta and whale shark sightings are seasonal and never guaranteed, check the season for this atoll rather than trusting a brochure photo.

places.name: Uninhabited Sandbank Picnic Island
places.note: Genuinely just sand and water, no shade structures at most of these, bring your own umbrella. $80-150pp depending on whether lunch is included. Boat out mid-morning, back for lunch or dinner depending on package.

places.name: Dolphin Sunset Cruise
places.note: Dolphins are wild, sometimes they don't show, and operators won't refund for a no-sighting evening. Still a pleasant two hours on the water timed to sunset for $50-80pp.

places.name: Sunset Fishing on Traditional Dhoni
places.note: 2-3 hours, $60-90pp. You are usually not keeping the fish for dinner, ask upfront if that matters to you.

places.name: Resort Spa Treatment
places.note: 60-90 min, $150-300 per treatment. Genuinely good quality but priced like Manhattan, not a beach town.

places.name: Day Trip to Male City
places.note: Skip for this trip. Male is a working capital with little for a beach-focused itinerary, and the boat transfer burns a window you don't have to spare in six nights.

places.name: Uninhabited Sandbank Picnic Island (South Male Atoll)
places.note: Exact sandbank varies by resort and tide, typically a 20-40 min boat ride out. Genuinely just sand and shallow water with no shade structures, bring your own umbrella or tent. Best between late morning and mid-afternoon when the tide keeps the bank exposed, some sandbanks disappear at high tide.

places.name: Snorkel Patch Reef Adjacent to Sandbank
places.note: Small reef patch often just off the sandbank itself, usually included free with the picnic trip since the boat is already there. Visibility depends on how many other boats are anchored nearby that day.

places.name: Beach Picnic Lunch Setup
places.note: Resort crew sets up a packed lunch, usually grilled fish, rice, and fruit, straight on the sand or under a pop-up tent brought by the boat crew. Quality is standard resort catering, not a restaurant experience, and sometimes included in the package price rather than charged separately.

places.name: Shallow Water Swim Loop Around the Bank
places.note: Waist deep turquoise water surrounding most of the bank, safe and calm for casual swimming or floating, no current to speak of most days. Nothing to see below the surface here, it is really about the color of the water.

places.name: Sandbank Aerial Photo Point
places.note: The classic drone shot spot, narrow curving strip of white sand with a color gradient in the water on either side. Every operator photographs from roughly the same angle so the pictures all look alike, worth doing once for ten minutes and no more.

places.name: Private Champagne/Snack Stop Add-on
places.note: Some resorts upsell a private table on the sand with sparkling wine and canapes before the group picnic, marketed as a proposal or anniversary add-on. Fine if you want the staged photos, skip if you'd rather just eat lunch with everyone else and save the fee.

places.name: Resort-to-Sandbank Speedboat Transfer
places.note: Usually departs mid-morning, 15-30 minutes each way depending on which sandbank the resort uses that season. Included in the picnic package price, not booked separately. Sea can be choppy outside the atoll's inner lagoon, ask staff if conditions are rough before boarding if anyone in your group gets

places.name: Local Fisherman's Island Market Stop
places.note: Skip. Some sandbank packages bundle in a stop at a nearby inhabited local island billed as a cultural market visit, but it is usually a short walk past a few souvenir stalls and a mosque, not worth the extra hour it adds to what should be a relaxed half day on the water.

places.name: Manta Point (Lankan Reef area, South Male Atoll)
places.note: Cleaning station that draws manta rays seasonally, roughly May to November when the monsoon current runs right, checked with your specific resort before you rely on it. Boat ride from most South Male resorts is 30-45 minutes. Snorkeling here beats diving for manta viewing since they cruise the surfa
places.neighborhood: South Male Atoll, outer reef channel

places.name: Guraidhoo Kandu (channel dive/snorkel site)
places.note: Strong channel current site, grey reef sharks, eagle rays, occasional turtles. Two-tank dive territory, not really a beginner snorkel site because of the current, ask your operator to grade it before booking if you are not a confident swimmer.
places.neighborhood: South Male Atoll, channel between Guraidhoo and reef

places.name: Turtle reef site (Kudarah Thila or equivalent house-adjacent outer reef)
places.note: Reliable green turtle sightings feeding on sponge and soft coral, less seasonal than mantas so a safer bet if the day only has one shot. Named site varies by resort operator, confirm exact location with your boat crew, several thilas in the atoll fit this profile.

places.name: Halaveli Wreck (or similar accessible wreck dive)
places.note: Sunk cargo ship now colonized by coral, a good add for certified divers wanting something other than reef and thila on the two-tank day. Skip if you are snorkel only, depth puts most of the structure out of surface view.

places.name: Resort dive/excursion jetty departure point
places.note: Where the dhoni or speedboat leaves for the outer reef, typically 8-9am departure for a full day out. Arrive 15 minutes early, gear fitting for divers happens here not at the site.

places.name: Whale shark point (South Ari Atoll, day-trip claim)
places.note: Skip for this trip. This is a real and famous whale shark aggregation zone but it sits in South Ari Atoll, a long boat transfer or seaplane hop from a South Male Atoll resort, it eats the whole day and often needs an overnight or seaplane add-on that this itinerary isn't built for. Some resorts sell

places.name: Reef gear rental kiosk (mask, fins, snorkel)
places.note: Rent here rather than pack your own if you're only doing one or two outer reef days, most dive centers include gear in the excursion price anyway so confirm before paying twice.

places.name: Eagle Ray Thila (or similar pinnacle dive site)
places.note: Underwater pinnacle rising from deep water, reliable eagle ray and reef fish density, a strong second-tank pick on the two-tank day. Current can be brisk near the top of the thila, this is a certified-diver site more than a snorkel one.

outings.why: Free, unlimited, self-guided snorkeling right off the resort, best at slack tide and in morning or late afternoon light; quality depends entirely on which resort's reef health you actually booked.
outings.name: House reef snorkel

outings.why: 30-60 min boat ride to a real reef site, snorkel or dive, this is the one day worth paying for; manta and whale shark sightings are seasonal and never guaranteed.
outings.name: Outer reef manta/turtle snorkel or two-tank dive
outings.season: varies by atoll, check season before booking on a manta phot

outings.why: Half-day boat trip to an uninhabited sandbar, gorgeous but genuinely just sand and water, bring your own shade because most sandbanks have none.
outings.name: Sandbank picnic

outings.why: Two hours out at dusk to look for wild dolphins; they sometimes don't show and operators won't refund for that.
outings.name: Dolphin sunset cruise

outings.why: Traditional-boat evening fishing trip, ask upfront if keeping the catch matters because usually you don't.
outings.name: Sunset fishing on a dhoni

destination.name: Maldives
destination.pitch: One resort, one reef, and a short menu of paid boat trips: this is a week of doing very little, well, not a week of exploring.
destination.caveat: It's genuinely one reef and one boat schedule for a week; if you need variety of place rather than variety of activity, this isn't it. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: One overwater or sandbank private dinner is worth doing once, but this isn't a food destination.
because.nature: Manta and turtle snorkeling on the outer reef, plus a real chance of wild dolphins at sunset.
because.adventure: The two-tank dive on the outer reef is the one genuinely active day, everything else is boat-and-float.
because.relaxation: A house reef at the door and a spa on-site means entire days with zero logistics.
